data.title: Clofazimine
data.summary: Antileprosy drugs · Riminophenazine dye; antimycobacterial and anti-inflammatory
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antileprosy drugs_

**Class:** Riminophenazine dye; antimycobacterial and anti-inflammatory

## Mechanism of action
- Binds guanine bases of mycobacterial DNA → inhibits replication; generates reactive oxygen species (weakly bactericidal)
- Anti-inflammatory: inhibits neutrophil motility and lymphocyte proliferation; stimulates phagocyte activity
- Very lipophilic — accumulates in fat and macrophages (crystals in tissues)

## Pharmacokinetics
- Variable absorption, better with food; very long half-life (about 70 days); stored in fat and reticuloendothelial system

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Leprosy — part of MB-MDT (and now 3-drug PB regimen)
- Erythema nodosum leprosum (steroid-sparing for chronic/recurrent ENL)
- Off-label: discoid lupus, pyoderma gangrenosum, granulomatous cheilitis (Melkersson–Rosenthal), granuloma annulare, Sweet syndrome
- MDR-TB (newer regimens) and Mycobacterium avium complex

## Dose & formulations
- MDT adult: 300 mg once a month (supervised) + 50 mg daily
- ENL: 100 mg three times daily (300 mg/day) for no more than 12 weeks, then taper to 100 mg/day; takes 4–6 weeks to act — combine with steroids initially
- Capsules 50 and 100 mg, with food

## Adverse effects
- Reddish-brown to purple-black skin pigmentation (dose-related; most marked in lesions; fades over months to years after stopping) — may cause social stigma and depression
- Red-brown discolouration of conjunctiva, tears, sweat, urine, sputum, breast milk
- Ichthyosis/xerosis (especially legs)
- GI: abdominal pain, diarrhoea; crystal-deposition enteropathy with high doses (can mimic acute abdomen — splenic infarction rare)
- QT prolongation

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity; caution in pre-existing GI disease and long QT

## Drug interactions
- QT-prolonging drugs (bedaquiline, fluoroquinolones, macrolides)
- May reduce the effect of rifampicin slightly (not significant clinically)

## Monitoring
- Weight, abdominal symptoms on high doses; ECG if other QT drugs

## Pregnancy & lactation
Used in pregnancy within MDT (WHO); infants may be born with pigmentation (reversible).

## Viva points
- Pigmentation is the main side effect — counsel before starting
- Anti-inflammatory action used in ENL (300 mg/day max 3 months)
- Crystal enteropathy with high-dose use

_Sources: Khopkar ch.6; Wolverton 4e ch.40 (Miscellaneous systemic drugs — clofazimine). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
